steps.text: Cream vegetable oil and butter or margarine. Add sugars and blend well. Add eggs and vanilla. Sift dry ingredients and add above. Refrigerate dough for several hours after mixing.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).
Dough will be soft. Shape into balls. Dip in sugar. Place on greased cookie sheet. Flatten slightly with a glass dipped in sugar. Bake for 12 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I grew up eating cookies similar to this, we called them "Aunt Edna's Sugar Cookies". Her recipe was slightly different, it calls for shortening rather than butter and uses confectioner's sugar for all of the sugar, not half granulated. When made this way, you get a cookie so airy and crisp it literally melts in your mouth.

I'm deleting my entire review from April 3, 2014 to update it four and a half years later. As is, the recipe is pretty good. What I don't like is how sticky the dough is. It's not suitable for rolling and cutting. I thought it had too much oil so subbed it out for all butter. My results were very dry cookies. So I subbed half of the oil for an extra stick of butter and it was the same thing. The amount is important for soft, moist cookies.

After using this recipe for so long, I made some of my own changes. To combat the oiliness, I use an extra cup of flour. This makes the cookies a bit softer after they're baked and a bit easier to work with; I can roll it out to cut into with cookie cutters. I roll out sheets of dough between parchment then freeze them for a bit before cutting, otherwise I can't roll or bake shapes at all.

I use about a tablespoon of vanilla (preferably homemade) and a tablespoon of buttery emulsions. They're good without the emulsion and extra vanilla but with them, these cookies are OMG amazing. I also like to add a bit of vanilla flavored sugar (also homemade) when I'm creaming the sugars and fats together. 

I use these cookies for my little business that I'm just starting and have gotten nothing but positive comments about them. Thanks for the recipe! I'm sure I'll be using it for years to come!

Great sugar cookies. Very light crunchy, fragile and delicious. I’m an amateur baker, so I followed the recipe to the T except I added a half teaspoon more of vanilla. Cookies flatten out on their own while baking so easy on pushing down on glass dipped in sugar (spray glass with cooking spray often to get sugar to stick). Get as much sugar to stick on top of cookie for better sweetness if you like baked glazed sugar. Other wise if not enough just coat after baking but I like the baked sugar taste better. Make a small as you can because they do flatten out during baking. This one is my favorite sugar cookie recipe by far. And I have tried many. I’m crispy cookie fan not a soft one.

I have been looking for this recipe. I use shortening insead of oil. If one would use an ice cream scoop to drop the cookies on to the sheet and a flat glass to flatten them (which has been dipped into a sugar and cinnamon mixture)the process is easier than rolling. These cookies just barely have time to cool and become crisp before they are gone. There have been times that I have had to put the dough in the frig on warm day or when the kitchen is hot between baking time.

This is the best sugar cookie recipe I have tried. I didn't have cream of tarter so I didn't use it and I heard other can didn't use it so I figured it was OK. Used half the oil. Shortening instead of butter. And it says chill 3 hours. I didn't chill at all and it was great.

Thank you for this recipe, I halve it every year and it comes out perfectly. We are cookie cutter people, so we roll and cut and decorate as part of our holiday traditions. These hold up beautifully and the flavor is so good. I do substitute olive and/or coconut oil for the vegetable oil. And they do best when chilled as directed before handling.

This is the same recipe passed down for many years with my ex-mother-in-laws side of the family. It is the only sugar cookie recipe we make in my family.IF you use 1 cup of shortening instead of oil them do make the best rolled sugar cookies. I even use the butter flavored shortening sometimes. Also don't roll too thin or they will not come out soft when you bake them.
I made one small change - I swapped out the vegetable oil and used coconut oil. Wow, they were fantastic!!! They tasted buttery, crispy, but with a little tropical twist. Highly recommended!

I made this recipe, but I used 1/2 cup of oil, and I used 2 tsp of vanilla. I made the batter the night before christmas, and refrigerated the batter overnight. I rolled out the dough the next afternoon, and it was so easy to work with. I used this recipe for christmas cookies. I cut them out, baked them 350* for 8 min, and they were perfect. I frosted and decorated them and served them to family on christmas day. My family loved them and they took some home with them, and the rest were gone by bedtime. I was weary about this recipe because of some of the reviews, but I am so glad I used it, and will use it again next year. We love that these cookies were soft and not hard and crunchy.

This is the best sugar cookie I've ever had, let alone made from scratch. They remind me of the cookies I had from a bakery in my childhood. I love a good sprinkle sugar cookie (non pareils), so I dipped the rounded balls of dough in regular granulated sugar on one side and the other side, I dipped into the sprinkles. Then I flattened out with the bottom of a glass. They were so good!! I will be making this recipe for years to come. Tonya

I halved the recipe and they came out AWESOME. I've been looking for sometime for a recipe that would mimic those Pillsbury sugar cookies with the holiday pictures in the middle...those are SO good, never could find a recipe that came close. This one is about as close as I need to get! Delicious! I substituted Sweetex shortening for the oil and people thought I had bought them commercially, they didn't believe I made them! Excellent!
We used this recipe to make 400 sugar cookies to give to neighbors and they turned out delicious! We've gotten many texts about great they are!

Overly sweet with little to no flavor. These cookies have a very odd texture. Also, the dough is very sticky and hard to roll out. I also tried the icing used on the cookies it is the same overly sweet taste and a gritty texture.
I used margarine and shortening; always use margarine in baking. This is a wonderful cookie. Not easy to roll, but I rolled into balls and pressed with a fork.

I have looked all over in my cupboard for that small well worn recipe card that had this exact recipe on it... After searching in vain I decided to go online. THANK YOU FOR POSTING! This turned out just as it always has...perfect sugar cookies!
They were so moist and delicious! My mom took one bite and said this was the same recipe her mom used and asked me to print it for her. Thanks for sharing!
Delicious! Crispy yet chewy -- just the way a sugar cookie should be!
Oh my god! This recipe is absolutely wonderful! Everyone enjoyed them and gave me compliments.

Super yummy cookies. The reason for only 4 stars is because they are incredibly delicate. If you're looking to pack these as a gift or even ship them they will not servive. I brought some to work and they didnt even make the 5 mile trip. They were crumbles of yummyness when I opened up the tupperware.

These turned out great! They are not super sweet, went great with coffee! I did decorate half of them and they were awesome! I cut the recipe in half also and it turned out fine. I even had to leave the dough in the fridge overnight and it wasnt a problem. I tasted the dough before I baked it and it tasted kind of salty so it had me worried, but once they were baked we did not taste the salt. I think these may be the best sugar cookies ive ever had!
